source_review.notes: Checked all twelve references for identity, edition or revision, publication date, publisher, official status, and relevant scope. Official records confirm ISO 31000:2018 edition 2 remains published after its 2023 confirmation while edition 3 is only a committee draft; NIST SP 800-39, SP 800-30 Rev. 1, SP 800-37 Rev. 2, CSF 2.0, and SP 800-53 Rev. 5 are final or published records; and ISO/IEC/IEEE 42030:2019 is published and marked to be revised. Checked ACM's primary record for Cunningham's 1992 paper, the SEI/publisher record for the 2019 technical-debt book, and publisher or author records for architecture and decision-record foundations. Draft ISO material is cited only to qualify current-version status.

evidence: Defined the nine-field exception tuple, scenario likelihood, horizon, loss, expected loss, ranges, residual risk, principal, and interest before mathematical use.
Checked set, tuple, multiplication, range, exponent, probability, implication, and counterexample syntax for consistent scopes and GitHub-renderable delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Loss dimensions that cannot honestly be made commensurable remain a vector rather than being forced into one unit.

evidence: Recomputed 0.001 times 10,000 equals 10 and 1 times 10 equals 10 for the equal-expected-loss counterexample.
Recomputed the exercise case as 0.02 times 500 equals 10 and post-treatment 0.01 times 500 equals 5.
Recomputed the debt illustration as four changes times fifteen avoidable engineer-days equals sixty engineer-days.
Executed exception-disposition under Python 3.14.4 and observed all seven exact expected states with empty standard error.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Probability, loss, control effectiveness, and effort values are explicitly hypothetical rather than calibrated forecasts.

evidence: Verified equal products pL can coexist with different tail severity, certainty, reversibility, and obligations, refuting expected-loss equality to acceptability.
Verified that for p greater than zero and finite n, (1-p)^n remains greater than zero when p is below one, so no observed event cannot establish p equals zero.
Checked branch precedence so nonapplicability and alternative compliance are resolved before exception validity.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The finite classifier and counterexamples do not define a complete decision procedure or universal risk preference.
